_readme: Every number this card runs on. The scripts read it; nothing is typed twice.
model_state.py carries a fallback copy of all of it, so a broken or missing
file cannot cost a card. When it falls back, the card says so.
WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS CHOSEN:
everything under 'backtest' was fitted from real games by nfl_backtest.py and
committed by that workflow. Nothing under 'grading' was: those are decisions,
kept in their own section so which is which stays obvious. The preseason
conversion is measured, on 352 team-seasons.
WHERE TEAMS START, AND HOW THEY MOVE:
preseason.mode is 'market', so a team's week 1 rating is the sportsbook season
win total in preseason_2026.csv, converted to points. ratings.in_season_k is
how fast results take over from that: the in-season fit carries weight
n/(n+k) after n games. k was MEASURED, not chosen. Over 3,407 games the error
curve is flat from 8 to 14 and 10 sits at the bottom of it. Throwing the
preseason number away the moment a game is played (k=0) is WORSE than never
updating at all, by 0.54 points with a paired t of -3.84, so the prior earns
its place all season.
WHY THE GRADES ARE CAPPED:
backtest.calibration holds, per strategy, the line mapping what the model
claimed onto what actually happened. On the spread the slope is -0.03 with a
95% interval of -0.18 to +0.12: the model's stated confidence carries no
information about who covers. A letter is a claim about evidence, so a grade
cannot outrun the record behind it. nfl_picks.py applies the caps and the card
shows a star and the reason wherever one bites. Re-run the nfl-backtest
workflow and every grade recalculates; nothing is pasted anywhere.

_notes._what: CHOSEN, not measured. Everything under backtest.calibration was fitted from real games; these were decided. Kept side by side so which is which is obvious. Same values as the college card, so the two grade alike.
_notes.conf_a: calibrated probability, in percent, needed for an A on confidence
_notes.value_a: points of calibrated probability above the price's break-even needed for an A on value
_notes.w_confidence: how much the merged grade leans on confidence rather than value
_notes.conf_floor: a call less likely than this cannot be lifted above D by the price alone. Chosen at 40 unless backtest.conf_floor.measured says otherwise.
_notes.win_points: the OLD composite scale. Still computed and shown as the raw score, no longer the grade.

backtest.window: 2013-2025 regular season, 3,407 games, walk-forward against real closing lines

conf_floor.note: no bucket at the BOTTOM lost with its whole interval below zero, so there is no measured floor and the chosen one stands. The buckets that did lose outright were 50-100%, which a floor cannot reach
conf_floor.basis: moneyline bets, bucketed by calibrated probability, judged on return

record_notes.model_gap_early: our number against the closing spread, weeks 1 to 4
record_notes.model_gap_late: our number against the closing spread, week 5 onward
record_notes.total_model: our total against the closing total
record_notes.total_over: taking every over, which uses no model input
record_notes.moneyline: betting the outright winner, judged on return per unit staked
record_notes.moneyline_fav: the same, only where we take the favourite
record_notes.moneyline_dog: the same, only where we take the underdog

_notes.line_sd: our uncertainty about the true spread. The college card uses 7.0
_notes.margin_sd: margin scatter around the true line. The college card uses 15.0 at a total of 52
_notes.total_sd: points around the true total. The college card uses 13.3
_notes.total_bump: margin scatter widens by the second number when the total exceeds the first
_notes.wind_bump: and narrows by the second number at or above the first, in mph
_notes.win_points: the scoring scale this card originated; college carried it over unchanged

_notes.break_even: percent needed to profit at standard -110 pricing
_notes.game_sd: margin scatter used to turn a spread into a win probability
